To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
preservice teachers who engaged in a study abroad and international service learning program in rural South African experienced a literacy awakening.

the ISL study abroad experience in South Africa provided preservice teachers a “literacy-awakening” that led to a more nuanced and complex understanding of literacy and how it is used and valued in a global community.

PSTs experienced a “literacies awakening” that led to a shift in their understanding of the role of language and literacy as they related to their own teaching and learning and that this shift in thinking occurred as the result of a study abroad experience in South Africa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how PST become literate and how they develop a critical stance towards literacy.
the role of international service learning and study abroad in preparing preservice teachers for culturally responsive teaching.
how preservice teachers become aware of and engaged with literacy in global contexts, and what implications this has for their professional development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ISL study abroad experiences have the potential to help PST become more critically literate, which can be transformative for their future teaching.
the international service learning program provided a transformative learning experience for PST, which resulted in a “literacy awareness,” a heightened consciousness of literacies in the world.
the study abroad program was successful in helping PST become more literate in their understandings of literacies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PSTs’ experiences of the study abroad program and their reflections on those experiences helped them to see the complexity of literacies in the world.
ISL study abroad programs are powerful opportunities for PST to experience and reflect upon literacy practices in local and global communities.
the ISL program helped PST to see literacy as a human right and to imagine how their future teaching would be informed by this understanding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ISL study abroad can be an effective tool for developing critical literacy in preservice teachers.
ISL study abroad experiences can be designed to foster PST’s critical literacy awareness and humanizing pedagogies.
ISL study abroad experiences can be powerful for PST to become literate global citizens.
